And that al-Hakim began to gaze toward the east.
And when he saw Aries (Ares / Mars) that had risen on the eastern horizon,
he muttered with his lips and said:
"You have risen, accursed shedder of blood!
My hour has come."
Then those two sprang upon him from the ambush,
and they threw a cord around his neck and strangled him.
And they killed the youth with a sword,
and hamstrung the donkey.
And they carried his corpse,
and descended from the other side,
and brought it to his sister.
She, then, buried him in her house,
without anyone noticing anything that had happened,
except for her and those two murderers and their master.
Now the slaves of al-Hakim, when they waited until morning dawned
and he did not descend,
went up to the top of the hill and found the youth who had been killed
and the donkey that had been hamstrung,
but him they did not find.
And they left and went down to the palace.
And when the slaves and the nobles were perturbed,
his sister called them and said:
"Do not be perturbed,
because my brother told me beforehand,
'During these days there is danger of death upon me,
and I am going to go up to the hill,
and from there on foot depart into the desert,
and hide there for seven days, and then I will come.'
And the youth who was with him he himself killed,
lest he show the place to which he departed."
And when they were quieted,
she began to bring the nobles one by one,
and give them rich gifts and good promises.
And during these seven days she made them swear allegiance to the child, the son of al-Hakim,
and she called his name al-Zahir.
And for that elder son who was in Damascus, she sent and brought him, as if he were to reign;
and when he came to the city of Tinnis,
she put him in irons and imprisoned him.
And during those days she made a sign to the slaves,
and they laid hands on that emir who had conspired with her in secret,
and on {OCR?} those two slaves who had killed the caliph.
And they set up crosses for them,
and on one gibbet the three of them were impaled.
And she commanded heralds, and they proclaimed:
"These are they who acted treacherously against their master and killed him,
and God brought their iniquity upon their own heads."
Such an astonishing deed did this valiant woman perform!
And she destroyed her brother, who had wanted to destroy her.
And she considered further,
that if those wretches who fulfilled her wish should remain alive,
